answer: A prism anchors in the delta only with a fresh signal: a one-time hardware attestation minted inside a physical secure element, single-use and non-transferable, and the delta rejects any signal already bound to a key. Silicon emits one signal per chip and chip supply is inelastic, so a farm buying k prisms bids up unattested hardware against everyone else — the k-th signal costs more capital than the first, a bill fixed to physical chips that no software can split or rent in bulk. Break: leaked attestation keys.
